title: Add active execution check to prevent duplicate concurrent sync runs
description: Add a check to make sure that the update/sync process is not already running before triggering a new update run (both manually and automatically), preventing overlapping job executions and race conditions.
cause: Multiple manual UI clicks or automated cron/webhook triggers can start overlapping ingestion runs without verifying if a synchronization process is already executing, risking race conditions and duplicate snapshot writes.
plan:
1. Implement process/job execution lock checks in scripts/sync_drive.py and scripts/trigger_sync.py.
2. Ensure server /api/sync and Cloud Run Job invocations reject or cleanly queue duplicate concurrent runs with 'in_progress' status.
3. Add unit test verifying concurrent sync requests return status: in_progress.

title: Support adding and scaffolding new projects dynamically
description: Provide a streamlined CLI command or automated scaffolding workflow to add new project configurations (e.g. data/<my-project>/ with config.json, risks.json, issues.json, snapshots.json, driver_tree.json, knowledge.json) and integrate them into the ingestion pipeline and dashboard navigation.
cause: Adding a new project currently requires manual creation of 6 boilerplate JSON schema files in data/<slug>/ without schema validation or automated template generation.
plan:
1. Create scripts/scaffold_project.py accepting --slug, --name, and optional source metadata.
2. Generate validated data/<slug>/ baseline files adhering to Pydantic schemas.
3. Add unit test verifying scaffolded project loads cleanly into server and dashboard views.

title: Add the list of admins/owners to the setup --status output
description: Add the list of admins/owners to the setup.sh --status output so that operators and administrators can view who has admin or owner permissions in the environment.
cause: In setup.sh (and deploy.sh) run_list_mode(), gcloud projects get-iam-policy ${PROJECT_ID} is already fetched into ${tmp_dir}/project_iam.json (line 200), but the parser only checks DEPLOYER_ROLES for serviceAccount:${SA_EMAIL} (lines 306-315) and never extracts or prints human/group principals bound to roles/owner, roles/editor, or roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin.
plan:
1. In setup.sh (and deploy.sh) run_list_mode(), parse ${tmp_dir}/project_iam.json with jq to extract all user:* and group:* members bound to roles/owner, roles/editor, and roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin.
2. Emit state lines (iam_project_owners, iam_project_admins) via emit_state displaying the resolved comma-separated list of owners and admins.
3. Add unit test verifying --status output includes project owners and admins.

title: Easy tool to enable a user to update the risks sheet(s)
description: Provide a simple, validated CLI config tool (`scripts/pipeline.py --pull-config / --push-config / --set-primary-sheet / --set-team-google-sheet / --show-config`) so a user can pull `config.json` from GCS locally, edit it in `vi` (or pass flags), and push it back to GCS (`gs://monaro-risk-dev-data/<project>/config.json`) using GCP IAM, while keeping the web tier 100% read-only (`read_only = true` on the Cloud Run Web Service GCS volume mount).
cause:
1. Updating project source URLs (Stream 1: Joint Risks Sheet, Stream 2: Team Google Sheet, Stream 3: Drive Folder ID) currently requires manual gsutil manipulation.
2. In data/monaro/config.json, project.links.sheets and sources.googleSheets.sheetUrl can drift without an atomic helper that validates and synchronizes both fields.
3. Exposing a public/web POST mutation endpoint on the Cloud Run Web Service unnecessarily increases attack surface.
plan:
1. Zero-Write Web Tier Hardening (deploy/terraform/modules/cloud_run/main.tf): Set read_only = true on the Cloud Run Web Service GCS volume mount.
2. Security Validation (scripts/security_utils.py): Implement validate_google_sheet_url() and validate_drive_folder_id().
3. CLI Pull / Edit (vi) / Push Tool (scripts/pipeline.py): Implement --pull-config [file] (pulls config.json from GCS to local file for editing in vi), --push-config [file] (validates schema & URLs and uploads back to GCS), plus --show-config, --set-primary-sheet, and --set-team-google-sheet.
4. Tests: Add unit tests verifying --pull-config, --push-config validation, and GCS persistence.

title: Terraform apply 409 conflict: existing resources (artifac...
description: Terraform apply 409 conflict: existing resources (artifact registry repo, github-deployer service account, state and data buckets) in monaro-risk-dev
cause: Terraform dev state (monaro-risk-dev-terraform-state/terraform/state/dev) does not track existing GCP infrastructure, causing terraform apply to attempt to recreate existing cloud-run-source-deploy repository, github-deployer service account, and state/data GCS buckets, failing with HTTP 409 Conflict.
plan: 1. Import existing resources into terraform state using 'terraform import' or Terraform 1.5+ 'import {}' blocks for module.artifact_registry.google_artifact_registry_repository.docker_repo, module.iam.google_service_account.deployer, and module.storage.google_storage_bucket.*. 2. Verify with 'terraform plan' that existing resources match state without 409 conflict. 3. Document bootstrap import instructions in deploy/terraform/README.md.Resolution: Fixed resource address mismatch in import.sh (docker_repo, state_bucket), validated dev and prod Terraform syntax, and added comprehensive import & 409 conflict resolution runbook in deploy/terraform/README.md.
